entries.test: Public reporting and filings on Microsoft's stake in OpenAI as of May 2024, i.e. whether it held equity in OpenAI itself or only a profit-share in the capped-profit subsidiary.
entries.note: The hedge 'as far as I understand' is kept; it is not probability language.

entries.test: Reported terms of the Microsoft–OpenAI deal (about 49% profit share up to a cap), OpenAI's corporate structure, and whether the for-profit arm had reported any profit by May 2024.
entries.note: 'Cap' is the drafter's reading of 'a very complex point'; it fits the known capped-profit structure.

entries.test: Reporting on Microsoft's roughly $11B in OpenAI investment, its exclusivity terms, and its 2024 deals with other AI firms such as Mistral.
entries.note: The source says 'into Microsoft', which is plainly a typo for OpenAI.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI was selling products such as ChatGPT Enterprise and API services that competed directly with Microsoft's Copilot and Azure offerings as of May 2024.
Reporting on OpenAI's military-use policy and on Microsoft pitching or offering OpenAI tools such as DALL-E or Azure OpenAI to the US military.
The Information's May 2024 report on Microsoft's in-house MAI-1 model and its scale compared with GPT-4, together with Microsoft's Mistral partnership.
entries.note: He relies on The Information's reporting but states it as his own claim.

entries.test: Whether Microsoft was building alternatives to OpenAI by May 2024, such as the Mistral deal, MAI-1, and hiring Inflection staff.
entries.note: This is a characterisation, but it has a plain reading: Microsoft was pursuing alternatives to OpenAI. The 'maybe' clause about confidence is not asserted.
'Could matter eventually' is hedged and has no deadline. It is written in the third person but is the author's own words.
